dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/12/Text/5] The average age was 12.47 (SD = 1.02). T tests showed that the Chinese children (M = 10.30, SD = 6.41) had significantly higher overall CDI scores than American children (M = 8.42, SD = 7.36): t(1217) = 5.68, p < .01. Parallel results were obtained when we controlled for age. Among Chinese children, 20.8% had CDI scores at and above 15, and 6.2% had CDI scores at and above 20. The percentages for American children were 16.4% and 8.3%, respectively.
